get_state.description: Read the bulb's identity and channel state (search_devices); also the discovery probe. Reply: payload_formats.SearchDevicesReply.

mqtt_reset.description: Reset the bulb over MQTT (the CLI's --reset). Reported to return it to provisioning.

The bulb's Wi-Fi MAC, uppercase colon-separated, as returned by startConfigRequest or search_devices.

level.description: Brightness 0-100. The HA integration maps its 0-255 scale with int(x / 255 * 100).

set_color.description: Set an RGB colour; switches the bulb to its RGB engine (UDP). Colour bulbs only.

set_color_temperature.description: Set colour temperature on the bulb's 1-100 warm-to-cool scale; switches the bulb to its white engine (UDP).

level.description: 1 = warmest, 100 = coolest. The HA integration maps Kelvin with level = 1 + round((K - 2000) / 4500 * 99) over 2000-6500 K; the MQTT reference puts the ends at 2700 K and 6500 K. The real endpoints have not been measured.

set_factory_mode.advanced_reason: Undocumented mode on production firmware. Read get_factory_mode first so the previous value is known; a reboot is the only recovery anyone has reported.
set_factory_mode.description: Enter the firmware's factory/test mode (set_factory_mode). What it changes is not documented; get_factory_mode reads it back.

set_pwm.description: Drive the four LED channels directly, 0-100 each; volatile, exits on any persistent setter. For testing and effects, not for state a client expects to read back.

update_led_firmware.advanced_reason: Replaces the firmware. A generic ESP8266 image, or any image on a non-ESP8266 model, bricks the bulb with no software recovery; the only route back is serial flashing of a module whose pads sit under capacitors. Keep Sengled's own image or a known-good shim to hand and use only the model-specific images the open-source projects publish.
update_led_firmware.description: Tell the bulb to fetch a firmware image from an HTTP URL and write it to its OTA slot (UDP). The MQTT 'update' type does the same.

ota_url.description: http:// URL of a .bin the bulb can reach. The image must be built for the ESP8266 RTOS SDK ota_1 slot at 0x110000 on the ESP8266 models; the EMW3091 and MX1290 models take Sengled's own images only.

methods.notes: Send the search_devices datagram to 255.255.255.255:9080 (and to the directed subnet broadcast -- the HA integration sends both, twice each) and listen about 2 s. Each bulb replies from its own address with its MAC, IP, firmware version and channel state; the `MN` field carries the model code where present, and the reply contains `R`, `G` and `B` keys only on colour bulbs (a white bulb answers with `W` alone). Discovery does not cross subnets and Wi-Fi client isolation blocks it. A reply's `result.ret` is 0.

device.name: Sengled Wi-Fi smart bulbs (W11 / W21 / W31 'Smart Wi-Fi LED' family)
device.notes:
Sengled's Wi-Fi bulbs (A19 and BR30 "Smart Wi-Fi LED" bulbs, model numbers W11-N13, W21-N13, W31-N15, W31-N11, W12-N15, W21-U23 and kin) join the home 2.4 GHz network directly and were controlled through Sengled's cloud: the Sengled Home app, the Alexa skill and Google Home all went through it. That cloud has been failing since mid-2025. It was down for most of a week from about 18 June 2025, kept dropping through July, and on 1 August 2025 Amazon removed the Sengled Alexa skill permanently, citing "prolonged outages" Sengled had not resolved (PCWorld, 31 July 2025). Trade press reported in August 2025 that staff had gone unpaid since January and that the company was not answering customers (LightNOW). Sengled still existed as a company at the time of writing (2026-10), so this is `unsupported` rather than `shutdown`: the bulbs' only vendor service is unreliable and unacknowledged, and nothing official supports controlling them any other way.
Two local paths survive, and this spec documents both:
1. UDP JSON on port 9080. Every bulb that is on Wi-Fi answers small JSON
   datagrams -- {"func": "<name>", "param": {...}} -- with no
   authentication, whether or not it can reach Sengled. On/off,
   brightness, RGB colour, colour temperature and a state read are all
   here, plus discovery by broadcasting the state read. This works on a
   bulb paired years ago with the Sengled app, as long as it is still on
   the network. The Home Assistant custom integration in SengledTools
   uses only this path.

2. Re-pointing the bulb at your own MQTT broker. The bulb learns its
   "cloud" during Wi-Fi provisioning: the setup payload carries two HTTP
   base URLs, and the bulb asks the second one where its MQTT broker is.
   Hand it URLs on your LAN, answer two small JSON requests, run a TLS
   MQTT broker on 8883, and the bulb publishes its status and energy
   counters to wifielement/<MAC>/status etc. and takes commands on
   wifielement/<MAC>/update -- the same topics it used with Sengled.
   The bulb never needs to see the vendor again. This is the route
   SengledTools' setup wizard and the HA add-on automate.

The Wi-Fi passphrase crosses the setup AP RC4-encrypted under a fixed, publicly known key -- obfuscation, not protection.
FIRMWARE: the bulbs take an OTA image from a URL they are given over UDP or MQTT, into the ESP8266 RTOS SDK's ota_1 slot. SengledTools uses this to load a rescue shim and then Tasmota/ESPHome/WLED on the ESP8266 models (W31-N15, W31-N11, W21-U23); the EMW3091 (W11-N13, W21-N13) and MX1290/WF864 (W12-N15) modules are not ESP8266 and the route does not apply. Flashing is noted here as a capability and is not specified: a wrong image bricks the bulb.

openness.notes: Nothing published by Sengled. The UDP function set was found by probing the bulb (unknown names answer "function not find", which is how more were discovered); the provisioning exchange and the MQTT topics were recovered from the app and from captures by the SengledTools author. The HA add-on reimplements the server side and agrees on every endpoint and topic.

credentials.notes: The passphrase travels inside an RC4 envelope under a fixed key that is public, so anyone capturing the setup-AP exchange recovers it; treat it as plaintext for threat purposes. Post-setup control is unauthenticated on both channels: anyone on the LAN can drive the bulb over UDP 9080, and the bulb connects to the broker named in /bimqtt with no credentials, trusting whatever TLS certificate it is shown (both open-source brokers disable verification on the bulb side and the bulbs connect to a self-signed CA). The bulb's MAC is the only handle a client needs to keep and it is not a secret.
stored_on_device: timeZone and userID strings from provisioning

factory_reset.description: The power-cycle reset is the one every guide gives for this family and the one the SengledTools wizard tells its users to do first; the exact count differs between sources (five quick cycles per the support.com guide and the SengledTools README, ten per one retailer's guide), so start with five and repeat with more if no AP appears. The remote resets ride the control channels and are only useful on a bulb that is already reachable.
factory_reset.effect: Clears the Wi-Fi credentials and the cloud URLs and returns the bulb to its setup AP. A bulb pointed at your own broker will need the full provisioning again, including the URLs.

procedures.basis: support.com 'How to reset the Sengled Smart Wi-Fi LED bulb' (flash three, blink two); SengledTools README says 'flick the power switch rapidly 5+ times'.
procedures.indicator: The bulb flashes three times, then blinks twice; the Sengled_Wi-Fi Bulb_XXXXXX network appears shortly after.
procedures.name: Five rapid power cycles at the switch

steps.action: With the bulb on, switch it off and on five times in quick succession, ending on.
steps.expect: Three flashes then two blinks; the setup AP appears.

procedures.basis: SengledTools UDP reference lists factory_reset (alias set_factory_reset) answering ret 0; nobody has written down what the bulb does next.
procedures.name: factory_reset over UDP 9080

steps.action: Send the factory_reset command (commands.factory_reset) to the bulb's LAN address.
steps.expect: result.ret 0; the bulb drops off the network and hosts its setup AP.

procedures.basis: SengledTools CLI --reset publishes [{dn, type reset, value "1", time}] to wifielement/<MAC>/update; its effect is described only as resetting the bulb.
procedures.name: reset over MQTT

steps.action: Publish the reset message (commands.mqtt_reset) to the bulb's update topic.

methods.description: Reset the bulb so it hosts its setup AP, join the AP, and talk to UDP 9080 at 192.168.8.1: a handshake that returns the bulb's MAC, an optional router scan, then one RC4+base64 encrypted datagram carrying the home SSID and passphrase together with two HTTP base URLs, then an end message. The bulb joins the home network, POSTs to <appServerDomain>/life2/device/accessCloud.json, GETs <jbalancerDomain>/jbalancer/new/bimqtt, reads the broker host and port out of that reply, connects to it with TLS on the port given (8883 by convention) and starts publishing. From then on the bulb's "cloud" is whatever you answered with. UDP 9080 control works regardless of whether the MQTT half ever comes up.
methods.name: Setup AP, then point the bulb at your own broker

APList.description: Reply to getAPListRequest: the networks the bulb can see, under payload.routers.

fields.description: Uppercase colon-separated BSSID; used instead of the SSID when the SSID is not ASCII.
fields.name: payload.routers[].bssid

fields.description: Signal indication; the reference client clamps it to 1-4 bars, so the raw range is at least that.
fields.name: payload.routers[].signal

parse_rules: Send scanWifiRequest, wait about 5 s for the bulb to scan, then getAPListRequest; the list is empty if asked too early.

StartConfigReply.description: Reply to startConfigRequest. A JSON object whose `payload` carries the bulb's MAC on the first exchange and `result` on the repeat exchange that precedes setParamsRequest.

fields.description: Bulb Wi-Fi MAC, 17 characters, colon-separated. The handle every MQTT topic is built from.
fields.name: payload.mac

fields.description: true when the bulb is ready to take parameters (checked on the second startConfigRequest).
fields.name: payload.result

parse_rules: Treat a missing `payload` as a failed handshake and resend; the bulb drops datagrams while it is busy.

algorithm_steps: Serialise the whole setParamsRequest object to compact JSON (the reference client uses its JSON library's default spacing; the bulb parses either) and encode as UTF-8.
RC4 key schedule (KSA) over the 52 ASCII bytes of the fixed key string, then the standard PRGA with no bytes discarded.
XOR the UTF-8 plaintext with the keystream.
Standard base64-encode the ciphertext (with '=' padding). The resulting ASCII string IS the datagram: it is sent as-is to 192.168.8.1:9080 with no JSON wrapper around it.
A reply that parses as JSON is plaintext; otherwise base64-decode it, RC4 with the same key, UTF-8 decode and parse. Either way it must contain payload.result == true.
credential_encryption.key_derivation: Fixed key, the same for every bulb: the 52-character ASCII string MTlCaWppbmdTaGFuZ2hhaVdpU2VuZ2xlZEZpMjBBQUJBU0U2NA== used byte-for-byte as the RC4 key (it is NOT base64-decoded first, although it decodes to readable text). No IV, no salt, no MAC; identical plaintext gives identical ciphertext.

test_vectors.description: Computed from the algorithm above with the standard library; scripts/test_sengled_wifi_bulb_spec.py reproduces every one. Addresses, SSID and passphrase are placeholders.

softap.ssid_notes: The suffix is six hex-looking characters, presumably from the MAC; the mapping is not documented. Neither open-source client scans for or joins the AP itself -- both tell the user to join it -- and neither asks for an AP passphrase, so it is recorded as open; nothing confirms that directly.

steps.action: On a LAN host the bulb will be able to reach, run an HTTP server that answers POST /life2/device/accessCloud.json and GET /jbalancer/new/bimqtt as protocol_details.cloud_bootstrap describes, and an MQTT broker with TLS 1.2 on port 8883 that allows anonymous clients and advertises ALPN x-amzn-mqtt-ca (protocol_details.mqtt_broker_requirements). Note the host's LAN address.
steps.expect: curl -X POST http://<host>:<port>/life2/device/accessCloud.json returns the success JSON; the broker accepts a TLS 1.2 client with no credentials.

steps.action: Factory-reset the bulb (five rapid power cycles, see factory_reset) so it hosts its setup AP.
steps.expect: The bulb flashes, then an open Wi-Fi network named Sengled_Wi-Fi Bulb_XXXXXX appears.

steps.action: Join the Sengled_Wi-Fi Bulb_XXXXXX network. The client is given an address in the bulb's subnet; the bulb is 192.168.8.1.
steps.expect: The client can send UDP datagrams to 192.168.8.1:9080.

steps.action: Send the handshake datagram and read the bulb's MAC out of the reply.
steps.expect: A JSON reply with payload.mac (17 characters). Retry on timeout; the reference client uses a 2 s socket timeout here and 15 s afterwards.

steps.action: Optionally ask the bulb to scan for networks, wait about 5 s, then fetch the list (payload_formats.APList). Needed only to pick a BSSID for a non-ASCII SSID or to show the user a chooser.
steps.expect: The scan request is acknowledged; the list reply carries payload.routers[] with ssid, bssid and signal.

steps.action: Send startConfigRequest again and require payload.result to be true before sending credentials.
steps.expect: payload.result is true. Abort if it is not.

steps.action: Build the setParamsRequest object -- name, totalStep 1, curStep 1, and a payload with userID "618", appServerDomain and jbalancerDomain (both http://<your-host>:<port> base URLs, no path), timeZone (an IANA zone name or "UTC") and routerInfo {ssid, password} -- RC4-encrypt and base64 the whole JSON text as credential_encryption describes, and send that string as the datagram. For a non-ASCII SSID send routerInfo {ssid: "", bssid: <uppercase BSSID>, password}.
steps.expect: A reply (plaintext JSON or RC4+base64) with payload.result true. The reference client treats a timeout here as success and carries on; the bulb often answers nothing once it starts joining.

arguments.description: Fixed string "618" in the reference client; meaning unknown, the bulb accepts it.
arguments.name: payload.userID

arguments.description: Base URL the bulb will POST /life2/device/accessCloud.json to, e.g. http://192.168.1.50:57542.
arguments.name: payload.appServerDomain

arguments.description: Base URL the bulb will GET /jbalancer/new/bimqtt from. Usually the same host as appServerDomain.
arguments.name: payload.jbalancerDomain

arguments.description: Time zone name; the bulb later reports it back as the timeZone status attribute.
arguments.name: payload.timeZone

arguments.description: Home 2.4 GHz SSID (ASCII). Empty string when bssid is used instead.
arguments.name: payload.routerInfo.ssid

arguments.description: Uppercase colon-separated BSSID, only when the SSID is not ASCII.
arguments.name: payload.routerInfo.bssid

arguments.description: Home Wi-Fi passphrase, in the clear inside the RC4 envelope.
arguments.name: payload.routerInfo.password

steps.action: Send endConfigRequest. The reply is optional.
Leave the bulb's AP and rejoin the home network; the bulb's AP disappears as it joins.

Join the home Wi-Fi, POST to <appServerDomain>/life2/device/accessCloud.json, GET <jbalancerDomain>/jbalancer/new/bimqtt, open a TLS connection to the host:port in that reply, connect to MQTT anonymously as client id <MAC>@wifielement, and publish supportAttributes to wifielement/c/status and the first status set to wifielement/<MAC>/status.
steps.expect: Both HTTP requests arrive within about 180 s of endConfigRequest; a status message naming typeCode, identifyNO and supportAttributes follows on the broker.

steps.action: Confirm local control: send {"func":"search_devices","param":{}} to the bulb's new LAN address on UDP 9080, or broadcast it.
steps.expect: A reply with result.ret 0 carrying the same MAC as the handshake.

timing.notes: From the SengledTools wizard. The bulb drops datagrams while busy, so the reference client simply resends on timeout with no retry limit until the user gives up.

causes: Wi-Fi client/AP isolation or a firewall between the bulb's network and the host; test with curl from another client on the same SSID.
The SSID is 5 GHz only. The bulbs are 2.4 GHz (802.11b/g/n) only; a band-steered single SSID is the usual case.
The base URLs carried a path or a trailing slash the bulb mangled. Give a bare http://host:port; the add-on matches the paths by substring because some firmware mangles the request line.
Non-ASCII SSID sent in the ssid field; use the bssid form.
troubleshooting.symptom: The bulb accepts the parameters but never contacts the HTTP server.

causes: The broker refuses TLS 1.2, RSA key exchange or the x-amzn-mqtt-ca ALPN value; the bulbs' mbedTLS build (AWS IoT C SDK) needs all three.
The broker requires a username/password or a client certificate; the bulbs send neither (some firmware sends a username that is a query string, which breaks per-user ACLs -- use pattern ACLs).
The CA changed after pairing. Reissue the server certificate under the same CA when the host's address changes rather than regenerating the CA.
troubleshooting.symptom: The bulb reaches /bimqtt but never appears on the broker.

cloud.local_alternative: The primary method above: replay the setup-AP exchange with your own URLs. No account, no vendor.

methods.description: The vendor route: add the bulb in the Sengled Home app, which needs a Sengled account and Sengled's servers to be up. It performs the same setup-AP exchange as the primary method but with Sengled's own appServerDomain/jbalancerDomain, so the bulb ends up on Sengled's broker. UDP 9080 then works on the LAN regardless, which is how bulbs paired before the outages are still usable. Listed because it still intermittently worked in 2025; expect it to fail, and expect anything it sets up to stop working with the next outage.
methods.name: Sengled Home app pairing through Sengled's cloud

steps.action: Reset the bulb, add it in the Sengled Home app and give it the 2.4 GHz network.
steps.expect: The bulb joins the LAN and answers search_devices on UDP 9080 even when the app shows it offline.

setup.notes: A bulb already on Wi-Fi (paired with the Sengled Home app at any time in the past) answers UDP 9080 with nothing more to do. A new bulb, or one whose network changed, has to be provisioned; the Sengled app does that only through Sengled's cloud, which has been failing. The route recommended here replays the app's provisioning exchange over the bulb's setup AP but hands the bulb URLs on your own LAN, so it treats a small HTTP server and a TLS MQTT broker you run as "the cloud" from then on. Both open-source implementations have run it on real bulbs; this project has not.

rejoin.notes: No command rewrites the Wi-Fi credentials or the cloud URLs on a joined bulb; a new router, SSID or broker host means a reset and the provisioning exchange again. The reset itself can be triggered over the old network (UDP factory_reset, MQTT reset) if the bulb is still reachable, which saves the trip to the switch. Changing only the broker host while keeping the same CA is handled by reissuing the server certificate, not by re-provisioning -- the bulb re-reads /bimqtt on every boot.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. Every UDP function, the provisioning exchange and the MQTT topics come from two open-source projects whose authors ran them against their own bulbs (SengledTools and the Home Assistant local-server add-on); the add-on credits the former for the reverse engineering. Byte-level facts are therefore `reported`, not `confirmed`.

entities.name: Sengled Wi-Fi Light
entities.notes: Over UDP 9080. Offer rgb and color_temp only when the get_state reply carries R, G and B (white bulbs answer with W alone). Power is on when any channel's freq is 0; brightness is best read with get_brightness (0-100 %); the last-sent colour and colour temperature should be cached, since the reply gives channel levels, not Kelvin. Poll no sooner than 2 s after a command. The mqtt_* commands are the same controls on the re-pointed broker and are left unbound here because a consumer needs a broker and the bulb's MAC before it can use them.

artifacts.description: The UDP function catalogue, the setup-AP exchange and its RC4 key, the stand-in HTTP endpoints and replies, the broker TLS constraints, the MQTT message vocabulary, the model/module table. No code transcribed.

Independent server-side implementation: the two HTTP replies, the URL-mangling quirk, the <MAC>@wifielement client id and query-string username, the status array shape and supportAttributes handling, the topic ACL.

evidence.documentation_review: Read on 2026-10-11: HamzaETTH/SengledTools (master) -- README, the three docs/references files, INSTRUCTIONS_ADVANCED.md, the HA custom component, and the behaviour of its udp, wifi_setup, crypto, http_server, mqtt_broker, mqtt_client, command_handler and diagnose modules; FalconFour/HA-Sengled-Local-Server-AddOn (main, end of maintenance December 2025) -- README, CHANGELOG, its HTTP server, MQTT listener, device storage, certificate manager and Mosquitto config. The two agree on every endpoint, topic and payload shape; the add-on credits SengledTools for the protocol work. The RC4 test vectors were computed here from the documented algorithm. Manufacturer status is from PCWorld (2025-07-31), Inside Lighting (2025-06-23) and LightNOW (2025-08-15). The reset is from support.com's guide and the SengledTools README; the two disagree with a retailer guide on the count.
evidence.open_questions: The Kelvin ends of the 1-100 colour-temperature scale; the meaning and units of freq/value in channel reports; what config_state, bind_state and mqtt_state encode; whether the bulb validates the broker's certificate chain or the time field; what the accessCloud.json POST body carries; the setup-AP suffix rule; and whether the five-cycle reset is right for every model.

enter.notes: The running firmware fetches the image itself and reboots into it; there is no separate bootloader mode to recognise. The rescue shim that SengledTools loads first is what then hosts its own setup AP with a web flasher -- that is the shim's behaviour, not the stock bulb's, and is not specified here.

image.format: Raw application image for the ESP8266 RTOS SDK ota_1 slot (0x110000) on the ESP8266 models; Sengled's own images on the EMW3091 and MX1290 models.
image.notes: Sengled pushed updates by publishing an update URL on the bulb's MQTT topic; the UDP update_led_firmware function takes the same URL. SengledTools serves a .bin from its own HTTP server and waits up to 300 s for the download to start. Whether the bootloader checks a signature is not established; the ESP8266 models accept community images, which suggests it does not.

dfu.notes: Flashing Tasmota/ESPHome/WLED is documented by SengledTools for W31-N15, W31-N11 and W21-U23 only. It is out of scope here; this entry records that the OTA surface exists and what it costs to get wrong.

recovery.notes: Two slots exist (the image goes to ota_1 while the stock app runs from the other), which suggests an interrupted download keeps the old image, but nobody has reported testing it. A wrong image that completes bricks the bulb.

fields.description: Target bulb MAC (same as the topic).
fields.name: dn

fields.description: Attribute to set: switch, brightness, color, colorTemperature, effectStatus, scene, effect, group*, reset, update, timeZone.
fields.name: type

fields.description: New value as a string (an object for the group* types).
fields.name: value

fields.description: Sender's epoch time in ms. Whether the bulb checks it is unknown; the reference client always sends the current time.
fields.name: time

mqtt_topics.description: Attribute reports: full set on connect, then deltas. payload_formats.MqttStatusMessage.
mqtt_topics.name: Bulb status

mqtt_topics.name: On-time counter

mqtt_topics.name: Connect announcement

CommandResult.description: The result object every setter and most getters return.

fields.description: 0 success, 1 failure.
fields.name: ret

fields.description: Reason text on failure: 'function not find' for an unknown func, 'get brightness error' and the like for bad params.
fields.name: msg

MqttStatusMessage.description: Payload on wifielement/<MAC>/status, /consumption, /consumptionTime and the connect-time wifielement/c/status: a JSON array of attribute objects. See protocol_details.mqtt_messages.status_types for the attribute names.

fields.description: The bulb's MAC.
fields.name: [].dn

fields.description: Attribute name (switch, brightness, color, colorTemperature, colorMode, supportAttributes, typeCode, identifyNO, ...).
fields.name: [].type

fields.description: Attribute value as a string.
fields.name: [].value

fields.description: Bulb-side timestamp; small integers on some firmware, epoch ms on others. Not useful as a clock.
fields.name: [].time

parse_rules: Take the MAC from the topic, not from dn (the add-on does; dn has matched the topic in every capture).
Index attributes by type; later messages carry only the attributes that changed.

SearchDevicesReply.description: The result object of a search_devices reply (unicast or broadcast). Field presence varies by model: R, G, B appear on colour bulbs only; MN was seen by the HA integration and not by the CLI reference.

fields.description: Wi-Fi MAC, uppercase colon-separated, 17 characters; the topic handle.
fields.name: mac

fields.description: The bulb's current LAN address as dotted quad.
fields.name: ip

fields.description: Firmware version string; contains a model-shaped token like _W31-N15_ on some builds.
fields.name: version

fields.description: Model code (typeCode), when present.
fields.name: MN

fields.description: Integer; provisioning state flag, values not established.
fields.name: config_state

fields.description: Integer; cloud-binding flag, values not established.
fields.name: bind_state

fields.description: Integer; whether the bulb currently has a broker connection, values not established.
fields.name: mqtt_state

fields.description: Red channel level; with G and B, normalised to the largest gives the RGB colour. Absent on white bulbs.
fields.name: R.value

fields.description: 0 when the channel is driven; non-zero when off. Likewise G.freq, B.freq, W.freq.
fields.name: R.freq

fields.name: W.value

fields.description: 0 on success.
fields.name: ret

parse_rules: Read result.ret first; anything but 0 is an error and the other fields are absent.
Power is on if any present channel has freq == 0.
Colour capability: all of R, G and B present.

cloud_bootstrap.description: The two HTTP requests the bulb makes on every boot to whatever base URLs it was provisioned with. A stand-in cloud answers both and the bulb never notices. Any port works; SengledTools listens on 57542 and the HA add-on on 54448 -- the port is whatever the URL said.
quirks: Some firmware mangles the request line; the HA add-on matches 'bimqtt' and 'accessCloud' as substrings of the path rather than exact paths, and answers bimqtt before accessCloud when both appear.
SengledTools counts provisioning as complete only once both endpoints have been hit from the bulb's address within 180 s.
requests: POST <appServerDomain>/life2/device/accessCloud.json (a body is sent; its contents have not been documented and neither server reads it). Expected reply, HTTP 200 application/json: {"messageCode": "200", "info": "OK", "description": "正常", "success": true}

GET <jbalancerDomain>/jbalancer/new/bimqtt (POST also seen). Expected reply, HTTP 200 application/json: {"protocal": "mqtt", "host": "<broker IP or hostname>", "port": 8883} -- the key is spelled protocal, as the firmware wants it.

models.description: Model codes seen in typeCode and on packaging, with the radio module where a source identifies it. Capability (colour vs white) per model is not fully established; detect it at runtime from the search_devices reply.
models.identify_marker: SengledTools treats an identifyNO containing ESP8266 as 'probably flashable' and typeCode W31-N11 / W31-N15 as confirmed.
table: W31-N15 -- A19 'Full Color' RGBW; ESP8266EX module; Tasmota template exists; OTA shim route works
W31-N11 (W31-N11DL daylight) -- white; ESP8266EX; OTA shim route works
W21-U23 -- ESP8266EX; OTA shim route works
W12-N15 -- 100 W-equivalent colour A19; WF864 module (MX1290); OTA shim route does not work
W21-N13 -- EMW3091 module; OTA shim route does not work

mqtt_broker_requirements.acl: A bulb needs write on wifielement/+/status, /consumption, /consumptionTime (the add-on also allows /attributes and /state) and read on wifielement/+/update (the add-on also allows /command and /set).
mqtt_broker_requirements.authentication: None from stock firmware: no client certificate, no password; allow anonymous. Client id is <MAC>@wifielement. Some firmware presents a username of the form ?SDK=C&Version=3.0.1, which breaks per-user ACL rules -- use topic-pattern ACLs.
mqtt_broker_requirements.port: 8883 by convention; the bulb uses whatever /bimqtt said.
mqtt_broker_requirements.tls: Mandatory. TLS 1.2 only (the bulbs' mbedTLS build from the AWS IoT C SDK negotiates nothing newer); RSA 2048 server certificate; ECDHE-RSA/RSA AES-GCM and AES-CBC suites at a lowered OpenSSL security level; prime256v1; ALPN must offer x-amzn-mqtt-ca (what the bulb sends) -- a broker that ignores ALPN fails the handshake. Both reference brokers run a private CA (CN 'Local-CA' / 'Sengled Local CA') signing a server cert (CN 'broker.local' / 'sengled.local'); whether the bulb checks the chain is not established, but keeping the CA stable across re-issued server certs is reported to keep paired bulbs connecting.

mqtt_messages.consumption: wifielement/<MAC>/consumption carries {type: consumption, value: "<integer>"} and /consumptionTime {type: consumptionTime, value: "<integer>"}; the reference guesses energy and time-on counters, units not established.
mqtt_messages.envelope: Every payload, in both directions, is a JSON ARRAY of objects {"dn": "<MAC>", "type": "<attribute>", "value": "<string>", "time": <epoch ms>}. Values are strings even when numeric. Several objects may ride one message (colour temperature is sent together with switch "1"). Captures of the vendor cloud show an "Os$" prefix before the array on the update topic; the reference client publishes the bare array and bulbs accept it.
mqtt_messages.status_types: switch, brightness, color (R:G:B), colorTemperature, colorMode ("1" RGB engine, "2" white engine), online, version, productCode, typeCode (model, e.g. W31-N15), identifyNO (module/chip marker, e.g. contains ESP8266 on the ESP bulbs), ip, deviceRssi, saveFlag, timeZone, supportAttributes (comma-separated list of the attributes the bulb implements, published to wifielement/c/status on connect). The bulb publishes a full set on boot; later messages carry only what changed. The add-on ignores status messages with fewer than five attributes as partial.
update_types: color: "R:G:B" decimal, each 0-255 (the vendor reference also shows hex "FF0000"; the reference client sends the colon form)
colorTemperature: "0"-"100" (the reference says 0 = 2700 K, 100 = 6500 K), sent with a switch "1" object in the same array
effectStatus: "0" none, "7" audio sync, "100" video sync, "101" game sync (TV-strip products)
scene: a case-sensitive name such as Sleep, Read, TV, Sunrise, Dinner; effect: colorCycle, randomColor

groupSwitch / groupBrightness / groupColorTemperature: value is an OBJECT {switch|brightness|colorTemperature: "<string>", gradientTime: <ms>, deviceUuidList: ["<MAC>", ...]} published to the first member's update topic; untested by the reference client
gradientTime: optional transition in ms on ordinary objects
reset: "1"; update: "<http URL of a firmware image>" (see features); timeZone: "<zone name>"

protocol_details.out_of_scope: Zigbee Sengled bulbs (Element line, Z01-*, E11-*, E12-*; need the Sengled hub or any Zigbee coordinator), Bluetooth-mesh bulbs (B11-*), and Sengled Wi-Fi plugs/strips/diffusers, which share the MQTT vocabulary but have not been checked against this UDP surface.

udp_control.capability_detection: A colour bulb's search_devices reply has R, G and B keys; a white-only bulb's has W alone.
udp_control.discovery: Broadcast search_devices to 255.255.255.255:9080 (and the subnet broadcast); listen ~2 s; every bulb answers with its mac/ip.
functions: set_device_color {red, green, blue: 0-255 each}; set_device_rgb takes the same arguments and was seen answering nothing

set_device_colortemp {colorTemperature: 1-100}; the two reference clients disagree on the Kelvin ends (HA integration 2000-6500 K over 1-100; MQTT reference 2700-6500 K over 0-100). Sending colour temperature also switches the bulb to its white engine.

set_device_pwm {r, g, b, w: 0-100 each} -- drives the four LED channels directly. Volatile: not saved, 0-2 is off, >100 clamps, and any of the four persistent setters above exits PWM mode and reloads the saved state; search_devices keeps reporting the saved state, not the PWM output.
search_devices -> result {mac, ip, config_state, bind_state, mqtt_state, version, MN?, R/G/B/W {freq, value}} -- the state read and the discovery probe; see payload_formats.SearchDevicesReply
get_device_mode / set_device_mode {mode}, set_color_mode {mode} -- mode values seen 0 and 1, meanings not established
get_device_mac -> result.mac; set_device_mac exists, arguments unknown, no reply observed
get_software_version -> result.version (string); get_hardver exists, reply not documented
get_device_adc -> result.adc (float, e.g. 630.73); get_dimmer_info -> result {dimer, max, count, maxflag, mini, mini2_count, adc[]} -- the dimmer-detection ADC, meaning not established
get_factory_mode -> result.mode; set_factory_mode {} -- a factory/test mode, effect not documented, left advanced
set_device_light -- rejects empty params with 'get b error'; the argument set is unknown
update_led_firmware {ota_url} -- the bulb fetches the image over HTTP and writes it to the ESP8266 RTOS SDK ota_1 slot (0x110000). See features.
udp_control.reply: {"func": "<echoed name>", "result": {"ret": 0, "msg": "...", ...fields...}}; ret 0 is success, 1 an error with the reason in msg ("function not find", "get brightness error"). Replies fit in 4096 bytes; the HA integration reads 1024.
udp_control.request: {"func": "<function name>", "param": { ...arguments... }}; `param` is always present, {} when the function takes none.
state_decoding: Power: on when any of R, G, B, W reports freq == 0; a channel with freq != 0 is off (the HA integration's reading; freq looks like a PWM period and value a duty, but neither source states units).
Mode: W.value > 0 means the white (colour-temperature) engine is active; otherwise the RGB engine.
Brightness: prefer get_device_brightness (0-100 %). Fallback: the largest channel value.
Colour: R/G/B values normalised to the largest of the three. Kelvin cannot be read back exactly; the HA integration caches the last requested value and otherwise estimates from the channel mix.
udp_control.timeout: 3 s in every reference client, one send, no retry. A client polling right after a command should wait about 2 s; the HA integration skips polls within 2 s of a command.
udp_control.transport: UDP unicast to the bulb's address, port 9080; the bulb answers to the datagram's source port. No framing, no checksum, no encryption, one JSON object per datagram.

remaining_unknowns: Colour-temperature scale endpoints: the HA integration assumes 2000-6500 K over 1-100 and the MQTT reference 2700-6500 K over 0-100; nobody has measured a bulb.
Channel report semantics: `freq` 0 is read as 'on' and `value` as a level, but neither source states units or whether freq is a PWM period.
The meaning of config_state, bind_state and mqtt_state in the search_devices reply, and of the mode values behind get_device_mode / set_color_mode.
Whether the bulb verifies the broker certificate at all (both reference brokers are self-signed and the bulbs connect); whether the CA must persist across re-provisioning.
The body the bulb POSTs to accessCloud.json, and whether any field in either reply besides host/port is read.
Whether the 'Os$' prefix seen on vendor-cloud update messages is ever required.
The energy units of consumption and consumptionTime.
Factory-reset count: five cycles (support.com, SengledTools) versus ten (a retailer guide); the blink confirmation is from support.com only.

Which W-series models beyond W31-N15 and W11-N13 are colour; the setup-AP SSID suffix rule; the OUI(s) of the Wi-Fi modules (not recorded here because the only MACs in the sources are the authors' own units).
Whether UDP 9080 answers while a bulb has no Wi-Fi credentials at all (it answers on the setup AP at 192.168.8.1 for provisioning; control functions there are untested).
